title: Hampton's record of Blue Because of You

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, he recorded your tune, also.
Yeah. Did he let you know he was going to do that?
No, I didn't learn about it until I heard it on 's session one night. I was coming home from the Gaslight.
And that's the first you knew about it?
That's the first I knew about it.
Well, he recorded it in like 1939.
And then you're talking about the seventies, and you didn't know?
I didn't know nothing about it.
I'll be damned. Seems like somebody would have mentioned that to you.

Only ones they mentioned -- I knew about Earl, we recorded it about two or three different times. Only others I remember was Fats Waller made it. And who else, somebody else made it. I forgot who it was now. I was surprised.
Do you remember who was on that record with him?
I don't remember. All I remember, you know, is Hamp's playing on it. I'd have to look it up. And that's the only time you've ever heard it?
Let me see what I can do about getting you a copy of it. Yeah, that-- in fact, that's the first time I heard the tune, was Hamp's record. I hadn't
heard Earl's record of it. But I was familiar with Hamp's record of it. And I didn't know that you two had this long --
Yeah, we raised up together. Hamp, Milt Hinton, and myself. We was all raised up down on Rose Avenue.
